glossario.simples: Taking part in decisions by giving ideas and opinions and by following what happens.
The document of a person who is registered to vote. In Portuguese: {{título de eleitor}}.
The Senate's website where people can suggest laws and give their opinion.
A suggestion for a law that any registered person can send through e-Cidadania. In Portuguese: {{Ideia Legislativa}}.
A smaller group of lawmakers that studies a subject before the vote.
A written opinion, with an analysis of a proposal. In Portuguese: {{parecer}}.
A question open to everyone, so people can give their opinion. It is not a scientific survey. In Portuguese: {{enquete}}.
The lawmaker who studies a proposal and suggests changes to the text. In Portuguese: {{relator}}.
An open meeting to hear experts and the public about a subject.
A bill presented by the people, with signatures from voters.
A channel to complain, suggest, praise, point out wrongdoing or ask a public agency for something. In Portuguese: {{ouvidoria}}.
A law that guarantees anyone the right to ask public agencies for data. In Portuguese: {{Lei de Acesso à Informação}}.
A group in a public school with the school's leaders, teachers, staff, parents, students and the community.
A group that follows public health, with SUS users, the government and health workers.
{{Sistema Único de Saúde}} (Unified Health System): Brazil's public health system.
An association that represents the students of a school. In Portuguese: {{grêmio estudantil}}.
A form of government in which power comes from the people, who choose their representatives.
A lie that imitates real news. In Portuguese: {{notícia falsa}}.
Checking whether a piece of information is true.
Trying to scare people by saying that something terrible is going to happen.
A group of candidates who run together in an election. In Portuguese: {{chapa}}.
A single registration to use government services on the internet.

slides.titulo: Politics is not only on election day
slides.texto: You can give ideas, ask questions, complain and follow the work of the people who were elected. And you can **start early**!
Before you vote, it is worth **getting informed** about who is running.

itens.txt: See what the person has already done and what they propose.
Compare different sources. This site shows proposals and votes, always with a link to the source.
At **age 15**, you can already get your voter card ({{título de eleitor}}). But you can only vote from age 16.
Young people can request their voter card on their own, without their parents' permission.
In an election year, voter card requests stop 150 days before the vote.

slides.titulo: Share ideas and give your opinion in Congress
slides.texto: The Senate and the Chamber of Deputies have channels open to the public.

cards.txt: On the Senate's e-Cidadania website, anyone over 12 can suggest a law.
cards.mais: With 20,000 supporters in 4 months, the idea goes to a Senate committee. There, it receives a report. It is the Human Rights and Participatory Legislation Committee. You sign up with a gov.br account.

cards.txt: You can give your opinion on any proposal and point out its positive and negative points.
cards.mais: A poll is not a scientific survey. The rapporteur of the proposal decides whether to use the opinions.

cards.txt: Meetings where deputies and senators listen to experts and to society.
cards.mais: Many are interactive: you can send questions over the internet, on the Chamber's website or on e-Cidadania.

cards.txt: The people can present a bill to the Chamber of Deputies, with **signatures** from voters.
cards.mais: The Constitution requires “at least one percent of the national electorate, spread over at least five States, with no less than three tenths of one percent of the voters in each of them”.

slides.texto: You can also take part close to home and to school.

cards.txt: An **ombudsman** channel to point out wrongdoing, complain, suggest, praise or ask for something.
cards.mais: It is the Integrated Ombudsman and Access to Information Platform, run by the CGU (Office of the Comptroller General). The ombudsman offices of many public agencies use the platform.

cards.txt: Anyone can ask public agencies for information, without saying why.

dados.val: up to 20 days, plus 10 if needed

cards.txt: In public schools, it brings together the school's leaders, teachers, staff, parents, students and people from the neighborhood.
It exists in the city, in the state and in the country. It follows and helps plan public health.

slides.texto: You can **practice** participation from an early age.

cards.txt: It represents the students of the school. Its board is elected by the students in a direct and secret vote.
The Chamber of Deputies' website for children, with games, news and contests.
A make-believe election run by {{Plenarinho}}, open to all ages.
Students send in bills. The authors of the best ones go to the Chamber of Deputies to defend them.
cards.mais: In 2026, there was a special edition, held inside the schools. In 2027, the program goes back to its usual format.

cards.txt: Public high school students write an essay. The winners spend a week at the Senate.

dados.val: 27, one per state and the DF

cards.mais: In August 2026, the young senators approved 3 proposals. They become suggestions for a Senate committee to analyze.

quadros.txt: In the student council election, Ana supports Ticket 1. Léo supports Ticket 2.
Ana explains her reasons. Léo listens until the end, without interrupting.
Léo disagrees and explains his reasons. No one calls the other names or laughs at them.
When it is time to vote, each one votes in secret. No one has to tell how they voted.
The result comes out. The two are still friends and play ball at recess.

slides.moral: Disagreeing is part of **democracy**. No one can lose rights because of their political opinion, and the vote is secret.

slides.titulo: Before you share a news story
slides.texto: **Fake news** spreads fast. Ask these questions before you pass it on.

passos.txt: Check whether the website or the profile is well known and reliable.
Don't stop at the headline. Read to the end.
See whether other newspapers and websites also reported the news.
Be suspicious of messages that try to scare you, use too many strong adjectives or ask you to send them to everyone.
The Electoral Justice has {{Fato ou Boato}} (Fact or Rumor). The Chamber of Deputies has {{Comprove}}.
Even if you agree with the message.

slides.pergunta: At what age can you get your voter card?
slides.explica: From age 15, you can get your voter card. But you can only vote once you turn 16.

slides.pergunta: You got a scary message that says: “send this to everyone!”. What should you do?
opcoes: Send it right away, to warn everyone
Check it in other places and, when in doubt, don't share it
Send it only if you agree with it
slides.explica: An alarmist message that asks to be spread deserves suspicion. When in doubt, don't share it, even if you agree with it.
